admission.justification: Waiting, hand deletion and product deletion were weighed with grounds, and the choice binds every future copies run and the real-root deletion after landing.

alternatives.option: The product deletes copies under Completed or abandoned task notes through the completed-task rule, run by the architect on the real root after landing.
alternatives.reason: D17 and D39 asked for the deletion; D41 withdrew only the archiving of the two masters, and after L26 no code reads the copies.

alternatives.option: Wait for the commanding sprint archive hook.
alternatives.reason: The sprint holds sixteen rows in progress and nine in planning, so its archive is far away while the copies block nothing and serve nobody.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Sprint archival becomes near-term routine and copies can ride it without stranding.

alternatives.option: Delete the copies by hand outside the product.
alternatives.reason: Unaudited deletion has no reviewed dry run, no report and no generation-owner release for comparison snapshots.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Never for bulk deletion; single-file accidents stay operator judgment.

consequences: knowledge-copies gains the completed-task rule; comparison snapshots release through their generation owner; review and retained-code refs stay until archive.
context: Seventy-three dataset copies under the notes of completed masters had no route out: the copies command deleted under archived tasks only, and the commanding sprint with rows in progress keeps its archive far away.
